reason: The multi-disciplinary report accurately identifies immediate life-threatening risks: Grade 4 neutropenia (sepsis risk), Grade 3 CVA (neurological compromise), and metabolic derangements (arrhythmia, encephalopathy). These require urgent ICU-level monitoring, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and electrolyte correction. Risk stratification is appropriately conservative for emergency care.
evidences: Grade 4 neutropenia mandates empiric antibiotics and isolation per neutropenic fever protocols.
Cerebrovascular accident with deficits requires neuro checks and blood pressure management.
